cards.explanation: The answer is submit, friends. Paul says, "Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ." Notice who it's aimed at: one another. That's everybody in the church, so nobody gets to watch this one from the cooling rack.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "Wives, submit to your husbands as to the Lord." Those last four words are right there in the line: "…as to the Lord." He's got a whole picture coming to go with it, so hang on to your oven mitts.

The answer is Christ as head of the church, friends. Paul says, "…the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the church…" The comparison isn't a king or a CEO. It's Christ and the church, and Paul keeps coming back to that pair all through this passage.

The answer is True, friends. Paul calls the church Christ's "body," and says Christ is the one "…of which He is the Savior." Both ideas are packed into one verse. The picture is about Christ and His church, and He's the Savior in it.

The answer is just as Christ loved the church, friends. Paul says, "Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her". The love he points to is Christ's love for the church. That's a high bar.

The answer is glorious and without stain or wrinkle, friends. Paul says Christ wants "…to present her to Himself as a glorious church, without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish, but holy and blameless." Glorious is the word he picks.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "He who loves his wife loves himself." He's just said husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. So the love for his wife and the care for himself go together.

The answer is that he nourishes and cherishes it, friends. Paul says, "…no one ever hated his own body, but he nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ does the church." Nourish and cherish, that's a pair of words worth keeping. It's the kind of care you give something you'd never want to see hurt.

The answer is False, friends. In the line Paul quotes from Genesis 2:24, it says, "…a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife…" So it's the man who leaves, not the wife, and the two become one flesh.

The answer is Christ and the church, friends. Paul says, "This mystery is profound, but I am speaking about Christ and the church." He's been bringing Christ and the church into every part of this teaching. Here he says it plainly, so nobody has to guess.

The word is respect, friends. Paul says, "…each one of you also must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband." Husbands are told to love, and wives are told to respect, both said plainly. That wraps up his words on marriage.

The reason Paul gives is that this is right, friends. He says, "Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right." No long list of reasons, just that one. Sometimes a short reason is all you need.

The answer is True, friends. Paul calls the command to honor your father and mother "…the first commandment with a promise…" It's a line from the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:12). The promise is coming in the very next verse.

The promise is that things go well and life is long, friends. Paul says, "that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth." Two things are named: that it may go well, and that the life may be long. Both are tied to honoring your father and mother.

Paul tells fathers not to push their children to anger, friends. He says, "Fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath…" Provoke means pushing them toward anger. It's a short warning, and it's aimed right at the fathers.

The answer is in the discipline and instruction of the Lord, friends. Paul says, "instead, bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord." That's the instead of the warning. Don't provoke them, bring them up in what the Lord teaches.

The word is Christ, friends. Paul says, "Slaves, obey your earthly masters with respect and fear and sincerity of heart, just as you would obey Christ." So Christ is the one they're serving in it. That's a heavy topic, and Paul keeps pointing to Christ the whole way.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says to do this "…not only to please them while they are watching, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from your heart." So it goes deeper than when someone's looking. It's from the heart.

The answer is that the Lord will reward each one for the good he does, friends. Paul says, "…because you know that the Lord will reward each one for whatever good he does, whether he is slave or free." The reward comes from the Lord. And it's for each one, slave or free.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says the Lord "…will reward each one for whatever good he does, whether he is slave or free." So the reward isn't just for the free. It's for each one who does good.

Paul tells masters to give up their use of threats, friends. He says, "And masters, do the same for your slaves. Give up your use of threats…" The masters are the ones with something to give up. Threats are what Paul names.
Heaven is the word, friends. Paul says, "…He who is both their Master and yours is in heaven…" Same Master for the slaves and the masters. That's a good thing for everybody to remember.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "…there is no favoritism with Him." He says it about the Master who is both the slaves' Master and the masters' Master, and who is in heaven. It's a good line to end the passage on.
